correctness.rationale: u(x)=log(1+x)+(1-cos(log(1+x)))/4 is real analytic, u_prime=e^-t(1+sin(t)/4)>0, u_doubleprime=e^-2t[-1+(cos(t)-sin(t))/4]<0 for t=log(1+x). Price lambda(t) decreases, clipped demand min(e^t-1,1/lambda) increases, hence Theta=lambda/d is continuous strictly decreasing from infinity to zero and each Theta>0 has unique equilibrium. Binding inequality is sin t>4/(e^t-1). On every I_k=(2k*pi,(2k+1)*pi), k>=1, h has negative endpoints, positive midpoint and h_doubleprime= -sin t-4 e^t(e^t+1)/(e^t-1)^3<0, so two simple roots and a binding interval; negative-sine half-periods slack. Endpoint offsets asymptotic to 4e^-m*pi, and at equality Theta=(e^t-1)^-2, so consecutive cost threshold ratio tends to e^-2pi. Independently computed first five positive half-period crossings at high precision, first roots 6.2906136333,9.4244550324, and the last threshold ratio 0.00186744273170826 against e^-2pi=0.00186744273170799. Numerical roots cannot certify infinite alternation, which follows from analytic concavity.
